English: Stick Fence Pen
A rudimentary pen built with gathered sticks and brush, providing the most basic containment for livestock in unsettled steppe lands.
Wooden Kraal
A roughly circular livestock enclosure of wooden stakes and branches, sheltering larger herds and reducing losses among the Indo-Aryan nomads.
Wattle Enclosure
Interwoven reeds and saplings form a sturdy wattle enclosure, protecting livestock from predators and harsh weather, and supporting modest population growth.
Cattle Shelter
A covered cattle shelter built with woven mats and timber roofing, offering protection from monsoon rains and increasing herd resilience and clan unity.
Expanded Kraal
A significantly enlarged kraal with reinforced fencing, multiple pens, and basic watch posts, supporting a thriving nomadic population and healthier herds.
Guarded Yard
A well-patrolled pen with raised platforms for sentries and a dedicated night watch, greatly improving herd safety and boosting manpower reserves.
Village Kraal
A large, communal enclosure at the heart of the nomadic village, with earthwork ditches and communal granaries, supporting great expansion and organization.
Elders Pen
A prestigious enclosure adjacent to the council tent, where the tribal elders oversee prized stock, inspiring loyalty and efficient resource management.
Chiefs Kraal
A fortified kraal reserved for the chieftains herds, surrounded by a retinue of loyal guards and council, symbolizing authority, unity, and prosperity.
Indo-Aryan Grand Kraal
The ultimate symbol of Indo-Aryan nomadism: a vast, semi-permanent kraal with monumental timber gates, ceremonial stones, and central assembly grounds, supporting a legendary population and unity.
